use: The original engraving shows officers’ ranges, the short timber enclosure line and lighter buildings down the shore approach.
The author’s account describes a 75 by 50 yard enclosure built of felled trunks, with a ditch ten feet wide and deep.
Named Barlow Point during the first settlement. The government gazetteer records the same named historical site on Melville Island.
The archaeological assessment records the main enclosure remains at Barlow Point and gives an approximate 80 by 60 m total extent.
